AmeriCup|2022 Brazil]]|}} }} '''Anthony Miles Lamb''' (born January 20, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont Catamounts]]. ==Early life== Lamb moved to [[Rochester, New York]] at a young age. He attended [[Greece Athena High School]] in nearby [[Greece, New York]], where he competed on the basketball team under coach Jim Johnson. As a junior, Lamb averaged 20 points and 13 rebounds per game in leading the team to the Class A state final. He was the only returning starter as a senior and posted 30 points and 17 rebounds per game. Lamb led the team to a number-one ranking in New York and an appearance in the Section V Class AI final. He was one of the finalists for [[New York Mr. Basketball]] and was twice named Greater Rochester Player of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Abrami |first1=Alex |title=Passion for basketball drives UVM freshman Lamb |url=https://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/sports/college/vermont/2017/01/24/passion-basketball-drives-uvm-freshman-lamb/96953372/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Burlington Free Press]] |date=January 24, 2017}} ==College career== In his first game at Vermont, Lamb scored 23 points on 8-of-12 shooting and collected nine rebounds in a 94–70 win against [[Quinnipiac Bobcats men's basketball|Quinnipiac]]. This earned him America East Rookie of the Week recognition. He had his first double-double with 14 points and 14 rebounds against [[UMass Lowell River Hawks men's basketball|UMass Lowell]] on January 19, 2017. Lamb averaged 11.9 points and 5.2 rebounds per game as a freshman. He was named to the Second–team All-America East and America East Rookie of the Year.{{cite press release|url=http://www.americaeast.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=14000&ATCLID=211505570 |title=Vermont's Historic Season Leads to Sweep of Men's #AEHoops Major Awards |publisher=America East Conference |date=February 27, 2017 |accessdate=February 27, 2017}} Lamb missed half of his sophomore season with a foot injury.{{cite news |last1=Abrami |first1=Alex |title=UVM basketball's Anthony Lamb named America East player of the year; Becker also honored |url=https://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/sports/college/2019/03/08/uvm-basketballs-anthony-lamb-named-america-east-player-year/3102029002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Burlington Free Press]] |date=March 8, 2019}} He averaged 14.3 points and 5.0 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Abrami |first1=Alex |title=UVM men's basketball: Catamounts picked to win America East Conference |url=https://www.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/sports/college/2018/10/17/uvm-mens-basketball-catamounts-picked-win-america-east-conference/1673250002/ |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=[[Burlington Free Press]] |date=October 18, 2018}} Lamb scored a career-high 42 points in an 83–76 double-overtime win against [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]] on December 18, 2018.{{cite news |title=Lamb scores 42, Vermont outlast St Bonaventure in 2 OTs |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401085725 |access-date=April 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 18, 2018}} As a junior, Lamb averaged 21.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game and led Vermont to a 27–7 record. He was named [[America East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|America East Player of the Year]] and was an [[Associated Press|AP]] Honorable Mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].{{cite news |last1=Walsh |first1=Lauren |title=Lamb earns AP All-America honors |url=https://www.mychamplainvalley.com/sports/lamb-earns-ap-all-america-honors/1896428147 |accessdate=April 4, 2019 |work=My Champlain Valley |date=April 2, 2019}} Lamb was named America East tournament MOP after scoring 28 points in the championship against [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]].{{cite news |title=Lamb, Vermont deny UMBC repeat, win America East title game |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401121700 |access-date=April 4, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 16, 2019}} On November 16, 2019, Lamb scored 23 points including the game-winning shot over two defenders to take down [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]. This marked the first time Vermont beat a high-major program in over a decade. Lamb upped his point total from his previous outing by scoring 30 points including 25 after halftime on November 19, 2019, in a 61–55 loss to defending national champion [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite news |title=Diakite, No. 7 Virginia hold off Vermont, 61–55 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168197 |accessdate=November 20, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2019}} At the close of the regular season, Lamb repeated as America East Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url= https://americaeast.com/news/2020/3/6/2020-mbbawards.aspx |title= Lamb's Second Player of Year Honor Highlights 2019–20 Men's #AEHoops Honors |publisher=America East Conference |date=March 6, 2020 on December 2, 2020.{{cite web |title=Detroit Pistons Announce 2020–21 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-announce-2020-21-training-camp-roster |website=NBA.com |work=[[Burlington Free Press]] |date=November 23, 2020}} He was waived on December 14 after appearing in 1 preseason game.{{Cite the [[NBA G League]] after being drafted sixth overall in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|2021 NBA G League draft]].{{cite web |title=Charge Announce 2021 Roster |url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-announce-2021-roster/ |website=canton.gleague.nba.com |accessdate=January 25, 2021 |date=January 22, 2021}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2021)=== On February 25, 2021, Lamb was traded to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web |title=Lamb joins RGW from Canton Charge |url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/lamb-joins-rgv-from-canton-charge/ |website=riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com |access-date=February 25, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} At the end of the season, Lamb was named the [[NBA G League Most Improved Player Award|G League's Most Improved Player]].{{cite web |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/rio-grande-valley-vipers-anthony-lamb-named-2020-21-nba-g-league-most-improved-player/n-5674933 |title=RRio Grande Valley Vipers' Anthony Lamb Named 2020–21 NBA G League Most Improved Player |website=OurSports Central |date=March 18, 2021}} ===Houston Rockets (2021)=== On March 8, 2021, Lamb signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) after the Vipers were eliminated from the G League playoffs.{{Cite web|date=March 9, 2021|title=Rockets Sign Anthony Lamb to Two-Way debut on March 11, 2021, scoring three points and with one rebound in 13 minutes played. His appearance made him the first player from UVM to play in a regular-season NBA game.{{Cite web|date=March 12, 2021|title= Houston Rockets' Anthony Lamb drains 3-pointer, makes NBA history for On April 24, 2021, he was one of seven healthy players available for the Rockets and scored a career-high 21 points in a loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|date=April 24, 2021|title= Rockets' Anthony Lamb: Excels with 21 points from bench|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-anthony-lamb-excels-with-21-points-from-bench/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-04-25|website=cbssports.com|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426061628/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-anthony-lamb-excels-with-21-points-from-bench/ contract]].{{cite web|title=Rockets Re-Sign Anthony Lamb to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-anthony-lamb-two-way-contract|date=September 6, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 6, 2021}} He was waived on October 18 after appearing in 1 preseason game.{{cite web|title= Rockets Claim Garrison Mathews off Waivers |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-claim-garrison-mathews-waivers|website=NBA.com|date= October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} === Return to Rio Grande Valley / San Antonio Spurs (2021–2022) === On November 3, 2021, Lamb re-signed with the Rio Grande Valley Vipers as a returning player.{{cite web|title=VIPERS FINALIZE OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-finalize-opening-night-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2021|access-date=November 21, 2021}} He averaged 15.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game. On January 6, 2022, Lamb signed a 10-day contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] via the hardship exemption.{{cite web |title=SPURS SIGN TYLER JOHNSON & ANTHONY LAMB TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-tyler-johnson-anthony-lamb-10-day-contracts |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 7, 2022 |date=January 6, 2022}} He appeared in two games for the Spurs, and following the expiration of the 10-day contract, he returned to the Vipers. On March 23, 2022, the [[Houston Rockets]] signed Lamb to a two-way contract. He did not appear in a game, and became a free agent at the conclusion of the season.{{cite tweet |author=Houston Rockets |number=1506717458522165268|title=OFFICIAL: The Houston Rockets today announced they have signed forward Anthony Lamb to a two-way contract. |user=HoustonRockets |date=March 23, 2022 |access-date=October 7, 2022}} ===Golden State Warriors (2022–2023)=== Lamb once again joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. On October 5, 2022, Lamb signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On October 14, his contract was converted into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Anthony Lamb to Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-anthony-lamb-20221005|website=NBA.com|date=October 5, 2022|access-date=October 7, 2022}} On March 17, 2023, Lamb's deal was converted into [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=TT_Basketbol |number=2070568889428082908 |title=Anthony Lamb Türk Telekom’da!}} ==Personal life== Lamb is the son of Rachel Lamb, who gave birth to him at the age of 17. She is a Union Roofer after previously working as a CNA. He first met his biological father, Nate Larkins, in November 2017. Lamb has a younger brother, Timothy. Lamb has been public about his struggle with clinical depression, including suicidal thoughts.{{cite news |last1=Norlander |first1=Matt |title=The fight of his life: Vermont's Anthony Lamb opens up about getting through darkness on his way to greatness |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/the-fight-of-his-life-vermonts-anthony-lamb-opens-up-about-getting-through-darkness-on-his-way-to-greatness/ |accessdate=March 11, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} ===Rape accusation and lawsuit=== In 2021, Lamb was accused of committing [[rape]] while at the University of Vermont.{{Cite web |title=Myers addresses Lamb signing amid 2021 sexual assault allegations |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/bob-myers-addresses-anthony-lamb-signing-amid-2021-sexual-assault-allegations |access-date=2022-10-17 |website=RSN |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Keane |first=Sean |date=2022-10-03 |title=Golden State inks Lamb to training camp contract |url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2022/10/3/23385891/warriors-sign-anthony-lamb |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=Golden State Of Mind |language=en}} In December 2022, Lamb was named in a lawsuit against the University of Vermont where one of the plaintiffs, a fellow student-athlete on the Vermont swim team, alleged that she was anally raped by him; Lamb was not included as a defendant.{{cite web |last1=Andrews |first1=Kendra |title=Warriors' Anthony Lamb named in relation to Title IX lawsuit |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35219649/warriors-anthony-lamb-named-sexual-assault-civil-lawsuit |website=ESPN |access-date=January 12, 2024 |date=December 10, 2022}}{{Cite magazine
